question: Should the prepared-event and receipt schema changes land with this Gitcrawl stack, and what backward replay proof is required before merging them?
rationale: The patch appears internally correct, but choosing the durable ledger contract, stack order, and acceptable upgrade evidence is an architectural ownership decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Land the ordered stack with replay proof
options.body: Merge https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/550, then https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/554, then this PR after replaying current-main ledger data and validating the final contract against https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/563.

options.title: Split the ledger runtime change
options.body: Move the generic prepared-event behavior into a separately reviewed compatibility PR and keep this branch limited to the Gitcrawl receipt vocabulary and producer.

options.title: Pause until downstream live proof
options.body: Keep the stack in draft until the downstream cloud/parity consumer can demonstrate the finalized contract in its protected-main environment.

recommendation.title: Land the ordered stack with replay proof
recommendation.body: Merge https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/550, then https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/554, then this PR after replaying current-main ledger data and validating the final contract against https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/563.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the related Gitcrawl stack and authored the affected receipt and ledger behavior, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the landing decision.
